extracted.intended_audience: ORR staff, care provider facilities, child advocates, legal service providers, and public commenters on the NPRM
extracted.subtask_short: ORR care standards for unaccompanied children
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed regulatory standards governing medical care, child advocate roles, legal services, medication administration, and related procedures for unaccompanied children in ORR custody. Includes operational requirements for care provider facilities and expectations for ORR interactions, referrals, and notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medication policies and procedures (§410.1307(b)(9))
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities must have policies and procedures based on state or local laws and regulations to ensure the safe, discreet, and confidential provision of prescription and nonprescription medications to unaccompanied children, secure storage of medications, and controlled administration and disposal of all drugs. A licensed healthcare provider must write or orally order all nonprescription medications and oral orders must be documented in the unaccompanied child's file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes adherence to applicable state/local law and documentation requirements for oral orders; requires secure storage, discreet/confidential provision, and controlled administration/disposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical isolation/quarantine limits and services (§410.1307(b)(10))
rubrics_metrics.description: Allows placement of unaccompanied children in medical isolation and exclusion from contact with general population when medically necessary to prevent spread of infectious disease due to potential exposure, to protect other children and staff, or as required under state/local/licensing rules, limited to only the extent necessary to ensure health and welfare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During medical isolation, care provider facilities must provide all mandated services under this subpart to the greatest extent practicable; children must be supervised under licensing ratios; when multiple children are isolated, they should be placed together when practicable given the nature/type of the medical issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement to ensure access to medical care (§410.1307(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR proposes that an unaccompanied child who requires or reasonably requests medical care will be placed in a care provider facility that has available and appropriate bed space, is able to care for the child, and is in a location where relevant medical services are accessible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This aligns with placing children in the least restrictive setting in the child's best interest and requires ORR to consider any specialized services or treatment required when determining placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer when appropriate facility not immediately available or needs arise
rubrics_metrics.description: If an initial placement meeting §410.1307(c)(1) is not immediately available or a medical need/reasonable request arises after the Initial Medical Exam, ORR shall transfer the child to a facility able to accommodate the medical needs; the care provider facility must immediately notify ORR when such a need is identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfers must follow subpart G processes, including submitting a transfer recommendation to ORR for approval within three (3) business days of identifying the need; aligns with requirement to move a child within ORR facility network to best meet individualized needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation and ancillary services for medical access (§410.1307(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities/ORR must ensure unaccompanied children are provided transportation to access medical services, including across state lines if necessary, and associated ancillary services to access specialists and geographically limited care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers transportation for specialists (neonatologists, oncologists, pediatric subspecialists), family planning, prenatal services, and care requiring heightened ORR involvement; ORR will review conflicts with state law to determine how to meet statutory responsibilities; ORR employees must abide by Federal duties when conflicts with state requirements arise within scope of employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitation of access to services requiring heightened ORR involvement, including abortions
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR must not prevent unaccompanied children from accessing healthcare services and must make reasonable efforts to facilitate access to services requiring heightened ORR involvement, including access to abortions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access is to be facilitated consistent with limitations on federal funding for abortions (Hyde Amendment) and in compliance with Religious Freedom Restoration Act, federal conscience protections, and other civil rights laws and HHS regulations; ORR will facilitate regardless of whether the Federal Government may pay under Hyde.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely notification to ORR of heightened medical service needs or pregnancy (§410.1307(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities shall notify ORR within 24 hours of an unaccompanied child's need or request for a medical service requiring heightened ORR involvement or the discovery of a pregnancy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is consistent with existing policy requirements for notifying ORR of significant incidents and services requiring heightened ORR involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of child advocates' role (§410.1308(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Child advocates are third parties who identify and make independent recommendations regarding the best interest of unaccompanied children based on information obtained from the child and other sources; they formally submit best interest determinations (BIDs) to ORR and/or the immigration court, which ORR considers but is not bound to follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Role codifies current policy-based functions and supports independent recommendations informed by parents, sponsors, agencies, legal providers, care providers, and health professionals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Child advocates' responsibilities (§410.1308(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsibilities include: visiting with clients; explaining consequences and potential outcomes of decisions; advocating for best interest regarding care, placement, services, release, and proceedings; providing BIDs where appropriate and within a reasonable time; and regularly communicating case updates with care provider, ORR, and/or other interested parties including post-release updates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies timely provision of BIDs to ORR, immigration court, and other interested parties and ongoing communication in planning and advocacy efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral, appointment timeframe, and termination of child advocates (§410.1308(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested parties may refer children for a child advocate; ORR would make an appointment decision within five (5) business days of referral except under exceptional circumstances; appointments would terminate upon case closure by the advocate, when the child turns 18, or when the child obtains lawful immigrant status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interested parties include ORR staff, immigration judges, DHS staff, legal service providers, care providers, healthcare professionals, and child advocate organizations; ORR considers available regional resources and availability of advocates when appointing; appointments limited to children currently or previously in ORR care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Child advocates' access to information and clients (§410.1308(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: After appointment, child advocates would be provided access to materials to effectively advocate, including in-person access to clients during normal business hours in a private area and access to all case file information with ability to request copies directly from care providers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May request copies without going through ORR's standard case file request process, subject to confidentiality requirements; advocates receive timely notice of any transfer of their assigned child.

rubrics_metrics.name: Child advocate confidentiality obligations (§410.1308(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Child advocates are required to keep case file information and information about the child's case confidential and are prohibited from sharing case file information except with ORR grantees, contractors, and Federal staff; they may conduct private communications with the child in confidential spaces (in-person or virtual).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed text aligns with TVPRA protections that child advocates shall not be compelled to testify or provide evidence concerning information/opinions received from the child; ORR seeks comment on ways to ensure confidentiality of meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-retaliation for child advocates (§410.1308(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR proposes that it would not retaliate against a child advocate for actions taken within the scope of their responsibilities, including disagreements with BIDs or advocacy on behalf of a child.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to be read consistently with ORR's authority to manage the unaccompanied children's program, including oversight responsibilities; presumption that advocates act in good faith.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal of legal representation and statutory framing (§410.1309 intro & statute)
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR strives for 100% legal representation of unaccompanied children to the greatest extent practicable and consistent with statute (TVPRA and INA); the Secretary must ensure, to the greatest extent practicable, that children have counsel to represent them in legal proceedings or to protect them from mistreatment, exploitation, and trafficking, with a preference for pro bono counsel but discretionary authority to fund representation where pro bono is impracticable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies statutory interpretation that there is no right to government-funded counsel but a duty to seek counsel 'to the greatest extent practicable' and preference for pro bono with discretion to fund non-pro bono services when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information, rights presentation, and confidential legal consultation (§410.1309(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: An unaccompanied child in ORR care should receive (1) a presentation on rights and responsibilities in the immigration system in the child's language and age-appropriate manner; (2) information about availability of free legal assistance and that they may be represented at no expense to the government; (3) notification about SIJ, juvenile court dependency/placement, asylum/other relief; (4) information about removal hearing rights and voluntary departure; and (5) a confidential legal consultation with a qualified attorney/paralegal/EOIR accredited representative. Communications with counsel must be private in an enclosed designated space (including virtual/telephone).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposes additional specificity beyond FSA requirements, including confidential consultations and explicit requirement for enclosed designated spaces for meetings with legal representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting legal rights information in preferred language (§410.1309(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Require that information regarding unaccompanied children's legal rights and access to services be posted in an age-appropriate format and translated into each child's preferred language in any ORR contracted or grant-funded facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent with proposed §410.1306; intended to ensure accessibility of information.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORR funding discretion for direct immigration representation (§410.1309(a)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent appropriations are available and pro bono counsel is impracticable, ORR may fund legal service providers to provide direct immigration legal representation to certain unaccompanied children (examples include URM enrollees without status, children appearing before EOIR/USCIS, continuity-of-service post-release within same service area, and other discretionary cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding is discretionary and subject to available appropriations; example list is illustrative not exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding for legal services outside immigration proceedings (§410.1309(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR may, subject to appropriations and discretion, fund legal services for protection of a child's interests in non-immigration matters such as ORR appellate procedures (PRP, risk determination hearings, denial of release), representation for children placed in long-term home care or RTCs, children with no sponsor, judicial bypass for medical procedures, state juvenile court representation for SIJ-classified children, and assistance obtaining employment authorization documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR invites comment on prioritization and on mechanisms to prevent zeroing-out of funding while ensuring capacity for influxes; funding subject to ORR judgment and resource constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectations for provision of funded legal services (in-person preference) (§410.1309(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: When ORR funds legal counsel, in-person meetings are preferred though telephone or teleconference are acceptable alternatives when privacy can be preserved; the child shall be accompanied to any in-person hearing or proceeding by the child's attorney of record/EOIR accredited representative or an ORR staff member or care provider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR considered but declined to require mandatory in-person attendance in all cases, striking a balance between access to representation and operational flexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing case files with legal representatives (§410.1309(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of proof of representation and authorization for release of records signed by the child or authorized representative, ORR would, upon request, share the unaccompanied child's complete case file apart from legally required redactions to assist with legal representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR recognizes proof of representation operationally via forms (e.g., Notice of Attorney Representation) but leaves flexibility for acceptable forms; emphasizes timely notice to representatives for effective legal advocacy, including in law enforcement events, age redetermination, and sexual abuse/harassment allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion and coordination of pro bono services
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR makes every effort to utilize pro bono counsel to the greatest extent practicable, provides lists of pro bono legal service providers by state and national organizations upon admission, and ORR-funded providers may coordinate referrals to pro bono services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledges that pro bono may be impracticable in times/locations of high demand and that ORR must be selective in funding services when pro bono is unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding for post-release legal services (§410.1309(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to available appropriations and ORR discretion, ORR may make funds available to relevant agencies or organizations to provide legal services to unaccompanied children who have been released from ORR care, including grants or contracts (potentially formula grants distributed geographically).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority intended to support continuity of legal representation after release; subject to appropriations and ORR program priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of good faith and non-retaliation for legal service providers (§410.1309(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall presume that legal service providers are acting in good faith with respect to advocacy on behalf of unaccompanied children and shall not retaliate against providers for actions taken within the scope of their responsibilities, including reporting harm or misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR retains authority to manage the program and ensure child's interests are considered in care and custody decisions; non-retaliation is balanced against ORR oversight duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Psychotropic medication administration standards (§410.1310)
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR proposes requirements related to the administration of psychotropic medications, stating that psychotropic medications should only be administered appropriately and in the best interest of the child and with meaningful oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes litigation context (Lucas R. v. Becerra) regarding 'drug administration class' and that ORR will be bound by any future court decisions or settlements; signals intent to adopt procedural safeguards and oversight for psychotropic medication use.
